transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, because it's probably not a huge deal. But what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting little things that I normally handle without any problem. 

Like, um, returning phone calls, or remembering to turn in a registration form, or even just stopping for a quick errand on the way home. I mean, everyone forgets things sometimes, right? But as a secretary, I'm usually the one keeping everyone else organized, so it's a little embarrassing to be dropping the ball on my own stuff. I just thought I should maybe ask someone about it, to be safe... Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless lately?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I haven't been feeling depressed at all. I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself when I forget things, obviously, but I'm generally a pretty upbeat person! 

I hope I didn't give you the impression that I was complaining too much or feeling sorry for myself? I'm mostly just a little embarrassed about dropping the ball lately. But my mood is completely fine, I promise. I'm just trying to make sure I'm doing a good job at work, you know?
When you notice the forgetting, do you also feel unusually anxious or worried?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say anxious. Not at all. I mean, I guess I get a tiny bit flustered right in the moment, just because I hate making mistakes, but I'm not... I don't sit around worrying about it or anything. 

I'm actually a pretty relaxed person! I just like to do things right, especially for my boss, so it mostly just bugs me a little bit when I slip up. But definitely no real anxiety or anything like that. Is that normal? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you also have trouble remembering things that just happened recently, like conversations or where you put something moments ago?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think so. I'm pretty good with conversations and keeping track of my things, like my keys or my phone. It's more just those... those little tasks or errands that slip my mind. 

I definitely don't feel like I'm losing my memory or anything scary like that. I can remember what someone just said to me perfectly fine. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than I need to. I'm sure it's just a normal thing, right?
Over the past two weeks, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, definitely not! I still love doing all my normal stuff. I'm actually really enjoying my weekends lately. I still love gardening and watching my shows, and spending time with my friends. 

I haven't lost interest in anything at all. I try to keep a really positive attitude about things. I hope that's what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful. I'm really not depressed or anything, I promise.
When did you first start noticing these forgetful moments?

Well, um... I guess it's really just been since I started taking this evening certificate program. That was about 15 months ago, I think? 

I mean, I've always been a really organized person—you kind of have to be when you're an administrative assistant! But trying to juggle my normal work with the evening classes... I just noticed that keeping my attention on everything and staying perfectly organized got a little bit harder to manage. 

It's really not that bad, though! I'm still doing well in my classes and everything. It's just a lot on my plate, so that's probably why those little things started slipping my mind more right around then. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you been worrying a lot more than usual about different things in your life?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, I have the normal stress of making sure I get my assignments done on time, but... no, I'm not sitting around worrying about things all the time. 

I try to be a really positive person! I think I handle everything pretty well, actually, all things considered. I hope that's okay to say? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right and giving you what you need. But yeah, no extra worrying or anything like that, I promise. Everything is generally really good!
Have these forgetful moments caused you any problems at work or in your daily life?

Well, um... I mean, I'm still getting by! I really am. I don't want it to sound like I'm failing at everything, because I'm definitely not. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... I have missed a few small follow-ups at work here and there. And maybe a couple of minor deadlines for my classes. It's nothing huge! But... well, I do worry a little bit that it might start to affect my reputation, you know? I'm really hoping to move up into an Office Manager role eventually, and I just want to make sure I'm doing everything perfectly so they see I'm ready for it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee! I really try my best every single day. I just want to be helpful and give you the right information. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you had any head injury or other medical problem around the time this forgetfulness started?

Oh, no, definitely not! I haven't hit my head or been sick or anything like that. I'm actually really healthy, thankfully! I make sure to take good care of myself so I can keep up with everything. 

So, no, no medical issues or accidents at all. I hope that's helpful? I know you have to rule out all those scary things, but I promise I'm perfectly fine in that department!
When you’re trying to focus on something, do you have trouble concentrating?

Um, focusing? Well, I mean, I can definitely focus! I'm really good at my job, and I can get things done when I need to. I don't want you to think I'm just staring at the wall all day or anything like that. 

I guess... sometimes, if it's a really long document I have to proofread, or if someone is talking for a really long time in a meeting, my mind might wander just a tiny bit? But I always catch myself! I bring myself right back to it. It's really not a big deal, I promise. I think everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, right? I just try my best to stay on track so I can do a good job. Is that what you mean?
Are these forgetfulness problems interfering with your ability to do your job or handle your usual daily responsibilities?

Well, um... interfering feels like a really strong word. I wouldn't say it's *interfering*, exactly. I mean, I'm still getting all my main work done, and I haven't gotten any bad performance reviews or anything like that! I always make sure the important things are taken care of.

I guess... sometimes it just takes me a little longer to get through my tasks than it used to? Or I have to double-check my notes a lot more just to be absolutely sure I didn't miss a step. But I always figure it out! I really don't want it to sound like I can't handle my job, because I definitely can. I just... I might have to work a little harder behind the scenes to keep all the plates spinning, if that makes sense? 

I really hope I'm explaining this right. I just want to be honest with you without making it sound worse than it actually is. Does that answer your question okay?
Do you find yourself frequently tense or on edge?

Tense? Oh, no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm walking around on edge or anything like that. I try to keep a pretty positive attitude! 

I guess I can get a tiny bit stressed sometimes, just like anybody else, you know? Like if we have a big deadline at the office or if I'm trying to balance a bunch of different things at once. But I wouldn't call it being tense. I try really hard to just take a deep breath and push through it. I don't want to be one of those people who complains about stress all the time. I'm usually pretty good at just... keeping a smile on and getting it done. Is that what you were asking? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
When you forget to do something, is it usually because you got distracted before you could finish it?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I really don't want to sound like I'm scatterbrained or anything, because I really do try my best to stay focused and get everything done. 

It's just that, well, the office can get pretty busy. Sometimes if I'm right in the middle of something and just one phone rings, or if I hear people talking nearby, it can kind of pull me off what I was working on. Or even just... a random thought about something I need to do at home will pop into my head, and I get a little sidetracked before I can finish the first thing. 

But I think that's just normal office stuff, right? I'm sure everyone gets pulled away by things like that when there's a lot going on. I always try to get right back to my work as soon as I realize it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you been forgetting things people just told you a few minutes ago?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, being a secretary, listening to people is a huge part of my job, so I really try my best to be on top of that! 

I might need to jot a quick note down if my boss gives me a whole long list of instructions all at once, just to be safe, but I definitely don't just forget things right after someone says them. I always want to make sure people feel heard, you know? I'd absolutely hate for anyone to think I wasn't paying attention to them. So, no, I think my memory for conversations is actually pretty good! 

Is that the kind of detail you needed? I can try to think of an example if you want, but I really don't think that's a problem for me.
Do you find yourself worrying about lots of different things most days?

Oh, um, no, definitely not! I try to be a pretty optimistic person, really. I don't want to be a worrier or someone who brings everyone else down with, you know, constantly stressing over every little thing. 

I mean, sure, I might think about making sure the bills are paid on time or hoping my boss is happy with the reports I typed up, but that's just normal responsible adult stuff, isn't it? It's not like I'm sitting around agonizing over things all day. I always try to look on the bright side and just handle whatever comes up. I really hope that sounds okay? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm some kind of nervous wreck or anything.
Have other people at work or at home noticed that your memory is getting worse?

Oh, goodness, no. I really haven't heard anything like that from anyone. 

I mean, I'd be absolutely mortified if my boss or my husband thought I was slipping or couldn't handle things! I always try to make sure I'm staying on top of my responsibilities, and I think I do a pretty good job of keeping everything running smoothly for everyone. 

If I ever do misplace a file or forget to pick up milk on the way home, it's usually just a silly little slip-up that anyone could make. Nobody has ever pulled me aside or seemed concerned about my memory or anything like that. I really try to be reliable, you know? I hope that's the right answer... I just wouldn't want anyone to think I'm not doing my fair share.
Do you ever forget conversations or events that happened earlier the same day?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say so. I mean, I can always remember the important things that happen during the day, like what meetings I scheduled or what my husband and I talked about over breakfast. 

Sometimes, if it's been a really busy day at the office and I've been juggling a million phone calls, I might not remember every single detail of a casual chat I had with a coworker in the breakroom, but... well, that's just because my mind is focused on my actual work, you know? I try to prioritize the things that matter so I don't let anyone down. I definitely don't have blank spots where I just completely forget something that happened a few hours ago. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. I really do try to be as sharp as I can be.
When you forget something, is it because the information was never properly absorbed in the first place, or because you later can’t recall it even though you were paying attention at the time?

Oh, um, I guess I'm not entirely sure? I mean, I really try to pay attention when people are talking to me, especially at work. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm ignoring them or being rude! 

If I do forget something, it's probably just because, well, maybe there was a lot going on and I just didn't catch it right the first time? Like, maybe I was typing an email and someone asked me a quick question in passing. It's not like I'm staring right at them, listening intently, and then it just vanishes from my brain. I really do try my best to be a good listener and absorb what I'm told. 

I hope that answers what you're asking? I just want to be helpful and make sure I'm explaining things the right way.
On most days, do you find it hard to stop yourself from worrying?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I mean, I think I handle things pretty well, all things considered. 

Of course, I care about doing a good job and making sure my husband is happy, so I might think about those things, but... it's not like I'm sitting around wringing my hands or letting anxiety take over my whole day. I really try to stay positive and just focus on getting my work done and being helpful to the people around me. 

If I ever do feel a little stressed, it's just the normal amount that anyone would feel when they have a busy schedule, right? I definitely wouldn't say I have a hard time stopping myself from worrying. I try to keep a good attitude. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Do you worry about lots of different things most days?

Oh, no, not really. Like I was mentioning a moment ago, I really try to keep a positive outlook on life. I definitely don't have a whole list of different things I'm stressing over every day. 

I mean, I just try to take things one step at a time—like whatever my boss needs next, or what's on the schedule for the week. I try not to let my mind jump around to all sorts of negative things or worst-case scenarios. I really prefer to just stay focused on being helpful and getting my work done. 

Does that help clarify things? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
